anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet, the ESP32-C3 native USB pins are wired to the opposite net names: pin 27 (named GPIO19/USB_D+, the module's D+ pin) carries the net labelled USB_D-, and pin 26 (named GPIO18/USB_D-, the module's D- pin) carries the net labelled USB_D+. The USB-C receptacle J12's D- pins (A7/B7) and D+ pins (A6/B6) are on nets USB_D- and USB_D+ respectively.
anomalies.expected: The ESP32-C3 native USB D+ pin (GPIO19) must connect to the same net as the receptacle's D+ pins, and GPIO18 (D-) to the receptacle's D- pins; i.e. U1.27 should be on USB_D+ and U1.26 on USB_D-, matching J12's A6/B6 (D+) and A7/B7 (D-).

evidence.quote: Sheet /Microcontroller/ (mcu.kicad_sch): U1 right-side pins 'GPIO19/USB_D+  27' and 'GPIO18/USB_D-  26' with the net labels 'USB_D-' and 'USB_D+' applied to them (reversed).
Sheet /Microcontroller/ (mcu.kicad_sch): J12 USB_C_Receptacle_USB2.0_14P pins A7/B7 'D-' and A6/B6 'D+', wired to nets USB_D- and USB_D+.

anomalies.impact: The USB data pair is cross-connected at the MCU, so the USB-C port cannot enumerate or program the ESP32-C3; USB is described in the spec as the 'logic/programming supply', so this defeats in-circuit programming (board would still run from the barrel jack).

anomalies.observed: On the Thermocouples sheet, U3's chip-select pin (~CS, pin 6) is labelled CS1 and U4's chip-select pin (~CS, pin 6) also appears labelled CS1; the net CS2 (which the MCU sheet drives from U1 GPIO7) is not connected to any MAX31855 CS pin.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec each MAX31855 must have its own independent chip select: U2 → CS0, U3 → CS1, U4 → CS2.

evidence.quote: Each chip has its own independent chip-select: ~{CS} (pin 6) on U2/U3/U4 goes to separate nets CS0/CS1/CS2
Sheet /Thermocouples/ (thermocouples.kicad_sch): ~CS pins of U3 and U4 both labelled 'CS1'.

anomalies.impact: U3 and U4 would be selected together, so both drive the shared SO line simultaneously (SPI bus contention / corrupt reads) and channel CS2 is never addressed, causing thermocouple faults and incorrect oven temperature control.

parsed.summary: The drawing contains a likely anomaly at the MCU's USB interface (U1's native USB D+/D- pins are attached to the oppositely named USB_D- / USB_D+ nets relative to the USB-C receptacle), and a possible bridged chip-select (U3 and U4 both on net CS1), either of which would make the board behave differently from the specified design.
